display_name: Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet, Margaret River
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Margaret River's red gravelly loams force Cabernet Sauvignon roots deep, yielding concentrated blackcurrant and bay leaf that define Vasse Felix Filius Cabernet. Petit Verdot at 1% injects violet spice and extra tannic grip, lifting the blend beyond standard Aussie reds. At $26, it delivers Bordeaux-level structure from this maritime pocket.",
  "wine_summary": "Vasse Felix planted Margaret River's first Cabernet in 1967, setting the benchmark for structured blends here. Filius, their second label, sources estate fruit to highlight the region's gravel-driven intensity without flagship pricing. This mix of Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, 4% Cabernet Franc, and 1% Petit Verdot channels the area's low-yield sites into dark fruit depth and herbal precision.",
  "terroir_expression": "Red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay dominate Margaret River's 2,137 km² GI, stretching along the Indian Ocean cape from Dunsborough to Augusta. These fast-draining soils warm roots for blackcurrant ripeness while clay retains moisture against dry summers, building firm tannins and eucalyptus mint notes. Maritime fog and diurnal swings preserve acidity, tempering alcohol to balance the inky violet from Petit Verdot.",
  "vinification_summary": "Estate berries ferment in temperature-controlled tanks to lock in primary fruit, followed by malolactic fermentation—a bacterial conversion of sharp malic acid to softer lactic—that rounds tannins for earlier drinkability. The blend then rests 10-12 months in French and American oak, adding vanilla structure without overwhelming Margaret River's herbal core. These choices prioritize site transparency over heavy extraction.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled kangaroo skewers cut through the wine's firm tannins with gamey char, while blackcurrant mirrors bush tomato glaze. Nashville hot chicken's spice finds relief in violet lift and cooling mint, casual heat tamed by acidity. Seared duck breast with juniper berries aligns dark plum depth to fine-dining savory. Lamb shank tagine pairs clay-soil earthiness to preserved lemon tang, structure matching slow-braised tenderness.",
  "comparable_wines": "Cape Mentelle Cabernet Merlot — shares Margaret River gravel cassis and bay leaf, slightly softer from more Merlot. Chateau Montrose Le Colombier — Bordeaux second label with similar Petit Verdot spice and tannic frame at parallel pricing.",
  "style_profile": "Cabernet-led blend with full body, firm tannins, and violet-spiced lift",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink now through 2030 for NV; cooler vintages like 2023 evolve faster. Store cool and dark to preserve tannin integration.",
  "value_assessment": "$26 at Spec's undercuts Pepper Tree Margaret River Cabernet ($25) and Leeuwin Estate Art Series ($30). Critics' 94 James Suckling confirms density worth twice the price of basic Barossa Shiraz. Buy multiples—scores and structure beat competitors.",
  "market_position": "Steakhouse lists favor it for pairing punch under $40 glass-pour. US retail at Spec's targets Aussie enthusiasts scanning Bordeaux alternatives. Collectors skip for flagships, but casual Cab drinkers grab it for weeknight reliability.",
  "insider_take": "Overlook the 'junior' Filius tag—this outpaces many $50 Margaret River flagships in violet complexity from that 1% Petit Verdot. Barossa Cab fans miss the point chasing fruit bombs; here, gravel grip demands food. Skip if you hate herbs—bay leaf dominates.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 0,
